Reports Third Quarter Financial Results Net Sales Increased 8.5%, Driven by New Stores and Comparable Store Sales Growth of 5.9% in the U.S. and 1.5% in Canada ThriftIQ TM Rollout Expanded to 108 Stores; Company Launches Next Phase of Innovation with Patent-Pending Autotagger and Image Capture Company Updates Fiscal 2026 Outlook Bellevue, WA - November 5, 2026 – Savers Value Village, Inc. (NYSE: SVV) (the “Company”) today announced financial results for the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026 (the “third quarter”). Financial highlights for the third quarter (comparisons are to the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025) • Total Company net sales increased 8.5% to $463.1 million; constant-currency net sales 1 increased 8.9%; and comparable store sales increased 4.2%. • For the United States (“U.S.”), net sales increased 12.2% and comparable store sales increased 5.9%. • For Canada, net sales increased 2.5%; constant-currency net sales 1 increased 4.3%; and comparable store sales increased 1.5%. • Net income was $23.4 million, or $0.15 per diluted share. Net income margin was 5.1%. • Adjusted net income 1 was $25.5 million, or $0.16 per diluted share. • Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA”) 1 was $75.9 million, a year-over-year increase for the fourth consecutive quarter, and Adjusted EBITDA margin 1 was 16.4%. “We are proud of our strong third quarter results, which marked our fourth consecutive quarter of year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth,” said Mark Walsh, Chief Executive Officer. “We are pleased with continued strength in our U.S. business, encouraging signs of improvement in Canada, and stronger than expected profitability in our new stores. Our innovation agenda is also gaining momentum, with continued favorable results from the rollout of ThriftIQ and our announcement today of the launch of our patent-pending Autotagger and image capture. We are excited to host the investment community at our upcoming Innovation Day in Minneapolis on November 10.” 1 Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin, as well as constant-currency net sales, are not measures recognized under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). For additional information on our use of non-GAAP financial measures, see “Non-GAAP Financial Measures,” “Constant Currency” and the accompanying financial tables which reconcile GAAP financial measures to these non-GAAP measures. 1 Innovation During the third quarter, the Company expanded the rollout of ThriftIQ TM , its proprietary pricing platform, to 108 stores. Stores using ThriftIQ continue to demonstrate gross profit growth, with higher unit sell-through, larger baskets and stronger sales yields, and the Company expects to continue to deploy the platform across its U.S. and Canadian locations through early 2028. The Company is also advancing its innovation agenda with the introduction of Autotagger and image capture, patent-pending industrial engineering solutions designed to enhance labor efficiency. As previously announced, the Company will host an Innovation Day on November 10, 2026 at its centralized processing center in Minneapolis, Minnesota, where it looks forward to sharing additional information about ThriftIQ, Autotagger and its broader innovation agenda. Capital Allocation Consistent with its balanced and disciplined approach to capital allocation, the Company continued to take actions during the third quarter to reinvest in its business, strengthen its balance sheet and return capital to stockholders. • The Company opened 9 new stores, ending the third quarter with 384 stores, and recorded pre-opening expenses of $5.1 million. • The Company repaid $51.9 million of outstanding borrowings under its 2025 Term Loan Facility using cash on hand. The repayment resulted in a loss on extinguishment of debt of $0.8 million. • In connection with a secondary offering on August 11, 2026, the Company repurchased approximately 1.0 million shares of common stock at a total cost of approximately $10.0 million, excluding excise tax. This repurchase was separate from the Company's share repurchase program authorized in 2025. • As of the end of the third quarter, the Company had $60.1 million of cash and cash equivalents, $179.2 million available to borrow under its 2025 Revolving Credit Facility and total debt of $674.4 million. 2026 Impact & Sustainability Report The Company published its 2026 Impact & Sustainability Report covering its 2025 fiscal year. The report highlights continued progress in advancing its sustainability initiatives, including sourcing nearly all its supply locally to support nonprofit partners and communities while helping minimize its environmental footprint; advancing innovation through ThriftIQ TM ; establishing policies supporting responsible artificial intelligence use; and leveraging team member feedback to strengthen the workplace experience. The report also highlights progress in reducing the Company’s environmental footprint through the conversion of additional GreenDrop ® donation locations to alternative energy sources, as well as partnerships promoting circular fashion. Other notable achievements include the completion of the Company’s first Climate-related Risks and Opportunities Assessment, continued reporting of Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, independent assurance of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions data, and enhancements to governance and reporting practices. Together, these efforts further the Company’s mission of making secondhand second nature. The report can be found at https://ir.savers.com/esg. Non-GAAP Financial Measures The Company reports its financial results in accordance with GAAP. Non-GAAP financial measures used by the Company include Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin. The Company has included these non-GAAP financial measures in this press release as they are key measures used by its management and its board of directors to evaluate its operating performance and the effectiveness of its business strategies, make budgeting decisions, and evaluate compensation decisions. Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are not calculated or presented in accordance with GAAP and have limitations as analytical tools. You should not consider them in isolation, as a substitute for, or superior to, analysis of the Company’s results as reported under GAAP. There are limitations to using non-GAAP financial measures, including those amounts presented in accordance with the Company’s definitions of Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin, as they may not be comparable to similar measures disclosed by the Company’s competitors, because not all companies and analysts calculate Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin in the same manner. Because of these limitations, you should consider Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin alongside other financial performance measures, including, as applicable, net income (loss) and the Company’s other GAAP results. The Company presents Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin because it considers these meaningful measures to share with investors as they facilitate comparison of the performance of one period with that of another period. In addition, by presenting Adjusted net income, Adjusted net income per diluted share, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin, the Company provides investors with management’s perspective of the Company’s operating performance. 4 The Company defines Adjusted net income as net income (loss) excluding the impact of loss on extinguishment of debt, IPO-related stock-based compensation expense, transaction costs, foreign currency exchange rate impacts, certain other adjustments, the tax effect on the above adjustments and the excess tax shortfall from stock-based compensation. The Company defines Adjusted net income per diluted share as Adjusted net income divided by adjusted diluted weighted average common shares outstanding. The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) excluding the impact of interest expense, net, income tax expense (benefit), depreciation and amortization, loss on extinguishment of debt, stock-based compensation expense, lease intangible asset expense, transaction costs, foreign currency exchange rate impacts and certain other adjustments. The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA margin as Adjusted EBITDA divided by net sales, expressed as a percentage. Constant Currency The Company reports net sales on a constant-currency basis in order to facilitate period-to-period comparisons of its results without regard to the impact of fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates. The term foreign currency exchange rates refers to the exchange rates used to translate the Company's operating results for all countries where the functional currency is not the USD into the USD. Because the Company is a global company, foreign currency exchange rates used for translation may have a significant effect on its reported results. In general, given the Company's significant operations in Canada, the Company's financial results are affected positively by a weakening of the USD against the CAD and are affected negatively by a strengthening of the USD against the CAD. References to net sales on a constant-currency basis indicate operating results without the impact of foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations. The Company believes disclosure of constant-currency net sales is helpful to investors because it facilitates period-to-period comparisons of its results by increasing the transparency of its underlying performance by excluding the impact of fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates. However, constant-currency results are not calculated or presented in accordance with GAAP and are not meant to be considered as an alternative or substitute for, or superior to, comparable measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. Constant-currency results have no standardized meaning prescribed by GAAP, are not prepared under any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles and should be read in conjunction with the Company's consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. Constant-currency results have limitations in their usefulness to investors and may be calculated differently from, and therefore may not be directly comparable to, similarly titled measures used by other companies. Constant-currency information compares results between periods as if exchange rates had remained constant period-over-period. During the thirteen weeks ended October 3, 2026, as compared to the thirteen weeks ended September 27, 2025, the USD was stronger relative to the CAD and weaker relative to the Australian dollar (“AUD”), which resulted in an overall unfavorable impact on our operating results. During the thirty-nine weeks ended October 3, 2026, as compared to the thirty-nine weeks ended September 27, 2025, the USD was weaker relative to the CAD and the AUD, which resulted in a favorable impact on our operating results. The Company calculates constant-currency net sales by translating current period net sales using the average exchange rates from the comparative prior period rather than the actual average exchange rates in effect.
